label: FP
reason: The user-provided header value is decoded and passed to doSomething, but the guard condition (500/42) + num > 200 evaluates to true (since 500/42 ≈ 11.9, plus 196 equals 207.9), so param is assigned directly to bar. However, the value of bar is never used in any output or response beyond being returned from doSomething. The sink referenced in the alert involves concatenation into a response via "+" operations, which occur only in the doPost method after bar is computed — but bar itself is not used in any string concatenation that would expose user input to the client. The only usage of bar is within doSomething(), which returns it, but there is no evidence of bar being rendered in HTML or injected into a response body. Thus, the XSS vulnerability claim is unfounded.

evidence.note: bar is assigned from param only if guard condition holds, but bar is never used in response
